properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-22, at the dev_reflow2 hub: "say that we get two projects that have duplicate or contradictory design content or implementations (as we are doing the adopt skill on many existing projects like in my brother's work hub, the chances of competing or duplicative work is very real). /brainstorm how the hub will flag this (is it automatic or will it only be discovered when a purposeful query is done and finds the issue)?"

═══ TODAY'S ANSWER, HONESTLY ═══
ONLY BY PURPOSEFUL QUERY. Nothing in reflow2 compares two designs unprompted.
· Within ONE design: the write guard warns or refuses near-duplicates at write time, and propose_heal sweeps for them on demand. Even so, Alex's work hub reports duplicate components still being written during ingest (fact:ingesting-a-real-workplace-corpus-costs-70-dollars-a-day-and-still-writes-duplicate-components).
· Across designs: cap:seam-incompatibility and pair_designs compare two designs, but only at INTERFACES, and only for a pair a person asserts. The hub trial found overlaps (the web-GUI duplicate check, the artifact-storage hole) only because a topic was asked.
· req:a-write-is-warned-when-the-same-thing-already-lives-in-a-related-design (accepted today) covers NEW writes, and only when the writing design knows its siblings. It does not catch (i) duplicates that already exist when two repos are adopted, which is exactly Alex's situation, or (ii) contradictions, which are not duplicates.

═══ THE DISTINCTION THAT SHAPES EVERYTHING ═══
DUPLICATION (two projects hold or build the same thing) is a similarity question. Mechanical signals catch much of it cheaply.
CONTRADICTION (two projects say incompatible things) is only meaningful where they SHARE something: an interface, a dependency, a resource, a data store, an actor. Two unrelated projects cannot contradict each other in any way that matters. ⭐ So contradiction checks can be SCOPED to shared anchors, which is what makes them tractable. Comparing every decision against every decision is not.

═══ WHEN IT COULD HAPPEN AUTOMATICALLY (ideas, none chosen) ═══
(a) AT WRITE TIME. Already accepted as intent. Covers new work only, and needs the child to know its family.
(b) AT ADOPT TIME. Adopt works region by region. Before writing a region, it asks every sibling design "who else has this?", the same fan-out the hub's pre-genesis duplicate check ran (0.24 s across two designs). This is the moment Alex's duplicates are born, so it is the highest-value moment. Also the cheapest: it narrows to one region at a time.
(c) WHEN A CHILD MOVES. The hub already detects that a child's committed design changed (upstream_status). With a kept baseline, it can diff what changed and compare only the NEW or CHANGED nodes against siblings. Event-driven, proportional to change, needs nobody to remember. ⭐ This is the answer to "automatic or purposeful": automatic, but triggered by change, not by a schedule.
(d) PERIODIC FULL SWEEP. The backstop for everything (a)–(c) missed, including overlaps that predate the hub. Expensive; run rarely, and report rather than nag.
(e) ON DEMAND. What exists today: the topic query. Stays useful for "is anyone already doing X?".

═══ SIGNALS, CHEAPEST FIRST ═══
1. IDENTICAL ARTIFACT CHECKSUMS across designs: the same file in two repos. Free, exact, and already recorded (reflow2 measures checksums). Catches copy-pasted implementations.
2. SAME EXTERNAL DEPENDENCY or SAME PUBLISHED INTERFACE declared by two designs. pair_designs already puts published↔published in `dead_surface`; for siblings that same bucket reads as "two projects offering the same contract", a possible competing implementation.
3. NAME / TEXT SIMILARITY of capabilities and components (the near-match guard's method). Noisy across vocabularies (the trial measured flo2 "collaborators" vs reflow2 "seats").
4. SEMANTIC COMPARISON by a model, ONLY on candidates from 1–3. Never a full cross-product; Alex measured ingest alone at ~$70/day.

═══ WHO IS TOLD, AND HOW ═══
Findings go to the hub's "what is owed" list as a cross-project overlap class, and to each owner's "what needs me". They are raised at a boundary (req:detecting-is-not-asking), never on every read. Each finding is a QUESTION to both owners ("merge, reference, or intentionally separate?"), because a flagged overlap is not automatically wrong.

═══ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea ═══
🛑 SOME DUPLICATION IS DELIBERATE: forks, redundancy, a declared mirror, two teams exploring alternatives. Without a way to say "yes, on purpose", a detector re-raises the same pair forever. It needs a recorded disposition (the acknowledgement mechanism already exists within one design).
🛑 SOME CONTRADICTION IS LEGITIMATE: two projects in different contexts may rightly choose differently (one on S3, one on git). Only a contradiction about a SHARED thing is a defect; everything else is information.
🛑 FALSE POSITIVES ACROSS VOCABULARIES will be common for signal 3. Flood the owners and the class gets ignored, which is how the within-design duplicate detectors lost trust before.
⚠️ COST: every sweep that uses a model costs tokens. The mechanical signals (1, 2) should run first and alone until their hit rate is known.
⚠️ THE HUB MUST REACH THE CHILDREN, and the children must export. hxm_program measured zero of seven siblings exporting.
⚠️ GATED: dec:the-hub-waits-for-somebody-to-ask-for-it (accepted) holds all hub BUILDING until a real user asks. Alex's field report (duplicates during ingest, $70/day) is arguably that ask. That is Anthony's call and not decided here.

═══ SIZE, as a finding not a ranking ═══
Signal 1 (checksums) at trigger (c) is small and exact. (b) adopt-time is medium and hits the root of Alex's problem. (d) and signal 4 are the expensive ones and should follow evidence from the cheap ones.
properties.name: OPEN — when two projects under a hub duplicate or contradict each other (likely when adopt is run across many existing repos), does the hub find out automatically, or only when someone happens to query the right topic?
properties.rationale: Recorded in reflow2's design: detection is reflow2 behaviour, and the hub holds no design of its own. Searched first with six read-path queries (duplicate/competing work across projects; contradiction between designs; adopt overlap; sweeps and periodic detectors; heal/duplicate detection). Read in full: Alex's 2026-09-21 ingest-cost field report (duplicates still written within one design), cap:seam-incompatibility (the only cross-design disagreement detector, interface-scoped, pair-asserted), and today's accepted write-time warning. The idea is kept separate from dec:idea-a-fact-has-one-home-across-a-family-of-designs-and-reflow2-enforces-it: that one PREVENTS a second copy going forward, while this one DETECTS copies and contradictions that already exist, including those that predate the hub. Adopting many existing repos makes the second case the common one.
